tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk that is not on top, relocate all smaller disks that sit above it to other pegs, ensuring the target disk becomes free.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 from peg 1 while disks 1‑3 are on top, first move disks 1‑3 to other pegs.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When assembling the final stack on a goal peg, place disks from largest to smallest, never putting a larger disk on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: While constructing the target configuration on a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To build [5,4,3,2,1] on peg 2, first move disk 5, then 4, then 3, and so on.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve a sub‑problem by moving the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the kth (largest) disk to its destination, then moving the k‑1 disks onto it, recursively.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For any Tower of Hanoi sub‑problem with k disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move 3 disks from A to C using B: move 2 disks A→B, move disk 3 A→C, then move 2 disks B→C.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Avoid moving a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger disks that must be below it have been placed; otherwise you will block later moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the goal stack, especially early in the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not place disk 1 on the goal peg before disk 5 is already there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Every move must satisfy two conditions: the source disk is the topmost on its peg, and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top is disk 2 is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains correctly ordered larger disks, never move them; treat them as an immutable base and only add smaller disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal configuration already has some disks in place.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg 2 already has disks 5‑3 in correct order, only move disks 2‑1 onto it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be moved onto any peg without violating size constraints; use it as a flexible placeholder to unblock larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk is blocked by smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to free disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full move list, simulate the moves from the initial configuration to ensure each move is legal and the final state matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have produced the move sequence, before output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Run a quick simulation of the 31 moves to confirm the final stack is on peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recognize Classic Single-Peg Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the initial state has all disks stacked on a single peg and the goal is the same stack on another empty peg, the optimal solution is the standard Tower of Hanoi sequence of 2ⁿ‑1 moves generated recursively.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the start of a problem, check if both initial and goal configurations consist of a single ordered stack on different pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: All 5 disks on peg 1, goal all on peg 2 → apply the standard recursive solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Generate Moves Recursively with Explicit Disk IDs
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use a recursive function that, for k disks, first generates moves for k‑1 disks, then emits the move of disk k, then generates the moves for k‑1 again, explicitly recording each move as [disk_id, from_peg, to_peg].
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list for any sub‑problem, especially after recognizing the classic pattern.
tower-of-hanoi.example: For k=3, source A, target C, aux B → moves: [1,A,B], [2,A,C], [1,B,C], [3,A,C], [1,C,B], [2,C,A], [1,B,A].

tower-of-hanoi.description: Violating size rule: moving a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget to check the destination peg's top disk size before moving.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always enforce the Legal Move Invariant: only move onto empty pegs or pegs whose top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk without clearing the path.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook that only the topmost disk can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the Clear Path for Target Disk principle: first relocate any smaller disks above the target.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Final configuration does not match the goal state.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop early, add extra moves, or forget to place some disks correctly.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Perform Post‑Construction Verification by simulating all moves and checking the final peg contents against the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Incorrect peg indexing (off‑by‑one or swapped pegs).
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Confusion between problem description (0‑indexed) and natural language (1‑indexed).
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Explicitly map the pegs as given (0, 1, 2) and double‑check each move's from/to indices.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Premature placement of small disks on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving the smallest disk first without considering the required ordering of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal principle; build the goal stack from largest to smallest.
